cohort: The study included 14,312,619 deliveries in the United States between 2017 and 2020.
finding: Gestational carrier pregnancies, while rare and increasing, are associated with favorable pre-pregnancy patient characteristics but also mixed obstetric outcomes, including increased odds of preterm delivery, placental abnormalities, and postpartum hemorrhage, and decreased odds of cesarean delivery in singleton pregnancies.
mod_finding: Gestational carrier pregnancies were associated with decreased odds of cesarean delivery in singleton pregnancies.
